Summary

A Squarespace plugin that lets visitors search the existing trip catalog using an AI search. This is £2,500 fixed, with bug fixes and extra development afterwards at £100 an hour with each request or bug reviewed within one week and a timeline then agreed.

What you get

Catalogue indexingYour existing trips, read from your Squarespace site, indexed so the search understands destinations, dates, activities, prices and descriptions.
AI searchNatural-language search over that catalogue, returning the best-matching trips with a short line on why each one fits.
Search interfaceA simple search box and results list, embedded on the Squarespace pages you choose and styled to match your site, on phone and desktop.
InstallationInstalled on your site through Squarespace code injection, tested on live pages.
HandoverA short written guide: how it works, how new trips get picked up, and how to switch it off.

Not included

  • Monitoring, uptime alerts, error reporting or analytics dashboards
  • Ongoing maintenance and improvements

Agreement terms

Once signed by both parties, this quote is the agreement between the Client and Fohm (the Supplier) for the work above.

  1. Scope and changesAnything outside of the agreed delivery, or any change to it, is a change request: the Supplier reviews it within one week and confirms the cost and timeline in writing before starting. Approved changes are billed at £100 an hour.
  2. Client responsibilitiesThe Client gives timely access to the Squarespace site, the trip catalogue and the accounts needed, gives feedback within 5 working days of a request, and confirms it has the rights to all content supplied. Delays on the Client's side move the delivery dates accordingly.
  3. AcceptanceThe Client has 10 working days after handover to report, in writing, anything that does not match the scope, which the Supplier fixes at no charge. If nothing is reported in that time, or the plugin is used on the live site, the work is accepted. Later fixes are billed hourly.
  4. PaymentInvoices are due within 14 days. The Supplier may pause work while an invoice is overdue, and may charge interest and compensation on late payments under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998.
  5. Ownership and handoverWhen all fees are paid, the Client owns the code written for this project, and the Supplier hands over the source code, documentation and any credentials it holds, so the Client or another developer can take the work on. Until then the Supplier keeps ownership and grants the Client a licence to use the work. Open-source libraries and third-party services keep their own licences. The Supplier keeps its pre-existing tools and general know-how, and grants the Client a perpetual licence to use any of them included in the work.
  6. Third-party platformsThe plugin runs on Squarespace and third-party AI and hosting services. The Supplier is not responsible for their outages, pricing, policy or API changes, or for breakage those changes cause; fixes needed because of them are billed hourly.
  7. Security and dataThe plugin is built with reasonable care and common good practice, but no software is free of vulnerabilities. The Supplier does not warrant that the work is secure, uninterrupted or error-free, and is not liable for security breaches, data loss or unauthorised access, including through the platforms it runs on. The Client is responsible for its site, accounts, backups and compliance with data protection law. Where the Supplier handles personal data for the Client, it does so only on the Client's instructions and to deliver this work.
  8. AI resultsSearch results are generated by an AI model and can occasionally be incomplete or inaccurate. They help visitors find trips and are not a statement of availability, price or suitability; the Client's catalogue remains the source of truth.
  9. WarrantyThe Supplier warrants that the work will be carried out with reasonable skill and care. Beyond the acceptance period, the work is provided as is, and all other warranties are excluded to the extent the law allows.
  10. LiabilityEach party's total liability under this agreement is limited to the fees paid under it. Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits, bookings, revenue or data. Nothing here limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot be limited by law.
  11. TerminationEither party can end this agreement at any time with 14 days' written notice, or immediately if the other materially breaches it and does not put it right within 14 days of being told. On termination the Client pays for work done to the end date (the build at the share completed, hourly work at £100 an hour) and, once paid, receives everything produced to that point. The deposit covers work already done and is not refundable. Clauses 5, 7, 10, 12 and 15 continue after termination.
  12. ConfidentialityEach party keeps the other's non-public information confidential and uses it only for this work. The Supplier may name the Client and describe the work in general terms in its portfolio unless the Client asks it not to.
  13. Independent contractorThe Supplier works as an independent contractor, chooses how the work is done, and may use subcontractors while remaining responsible for their work.
  14. Events outside controlNeither party is liable for delays caused by events beyond its reasonable control, such as platform outages, illness or natural disasters, provided it tells the other party promptly.
  15. GeneralThis document is the whole agreement and replaces earlier discussions. Changes are only valid in writing (email is enough) agreed by both parties. Notices are given by email to each party's usual address. If any clause is unenforceable, the rest still applies. Neither party may transfer this agreement without the other's written consent. This agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction.
